blockers.title: SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is not fail-safe when the ambiguity removed the affected lane from that universe
blockers.subjectEvidence: The component-lane universe is 'exactly one component lane per declared component identity'. An ownerId outside that universe is AMBIGUOUS, while the preview default is SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE and the law says that option selects every lane in the closed universe.
blockers.counterexample: Let component A's current manifest/index declaration be missing, corrupt, or deleted while the ownership record or a deleted unit's previous claim still resolves to A. A is then outside the universe by the subject's own definition, which triggers AMBIGUOUS. The preview default selects the entire current universe, but that universe does not contain A, so A remains an affected omitted lane rather than being selected or causing refusal.
blockers.whyBlocking: The universe has no pinned snapshot rule and is not defined as the union of previous/current component identities and ownership claims. Therefore 'select all' is only safe after assuming away the declaration-loss ambiguity it is supposed to handle. This directly violates selector.failSafe and live DR-G16's no-waiver rule, so CODEX-V1-B2 is not repaired.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the component-lane universe over an immutable comparison basis that cannot shrink under the reviewed change, such as the validated union of previous/current index identities and ownership claims. If universe construction, a component declaration, or an ownerId is missing/invalid, SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE must be unavailable unless the missing lane is retained in that union; otherwise the only safe outcome is REFUSE. Add deletion/corruption fixtures proving the affected lane cannot fall outside the fail-safe set.

blockers.title: Dependency-edge and trigger-table omissions never enter ambiguity, so the selector still admits silent under-selection
blockers.subjectEvidence: authority calls the ownership record plus dependency edges the only impact authority, but shared-lane expansion uses a separate committed trigger table and selectorDecision digests it. The sole ambiguity test validates ownership records/ownerIds. No rule validates dependency-edge or trigger-table presence, uniqueness, completeness, parse/admission standing, previous/current union, or self-change. The corpus has C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD but no dependency-record or trigger-table mutation class.
blockers.counterexample: Omit A's declared A-to-SL-2 publisher row from the trigger table, then change an A-owned unit. The ownership record is complete and unambiguous, A is selected, but SL-2 is skipped and skippedLaneProof can truthfully say no trigger selected it. Likewise an absent/unreadable dependency edge can be treated as an empty current edge set because the algorithm never joins DR-103 refusal to AMBIGUOUS. Neither case reaches REFUSE or SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE.
blockers.whyBlocking: The trigger table is an unacknowledged third impact authority, and both it and the dependency graph can silently lose selection edges. Digesting inputs proves bytes, not completeness. This leaves the omitted-dependency/shared-surface failure that DR-121 and live DR-G16 explicitly require the contract to catch.
blockers.requiredRepair: Put every impact input on one closed authority roster. Define schema/custody, completeness, previous/current self-change expansion, and invalid/missing/conflicting behavior for dependency edges and the trigger table. Their ambiguity must REFUSE or select a universe proven to contain all prior/current lanes. Add forced dependency-record and trigger-table omission/conflict corpus classes, and make skipped-lane proof invalid unless all authoritative records first pass those checks.

blockers.title: A named blocked-on-ride standing can satisfy the signed-evidence class for preview-required selected lanes
blockers.subjectEvidence: signedPerLaneClosureEvidence and G16-4 accept either signed closure bytes/declarations or a named blocked-on-ride standing for every selected lane. independentRelease.evidence repeats the same alternative. No pass law says blocked-on-ride is non-success or prevents future G16 qualification; execution only says the design artifact's present existence does not QUALIFY.
blockers.counterexample: Select component A and SL-1 through SL-4, emit no signed closure evidence for any of them, and attach named DR-120/118/111 owners as blocked-on-ride. G16-4 and the independent-release evidence shape are satisfied as written even though the live G16 row's per-lane signed closure evidence is absent. The exception is not limited to D-002-deferred SL-5/SL-6 or deferred role/platform cells.
blockers.whyBlocking: CODEX-V1-B1 allowed an explicit blocked/preview-not-required slot only for D-002-deferred lanes; v2 broadens that escape to every selected lane. A blocked slot is useful accounting but cannot be acceptance evidence for a preview-required selected lane. Without a non-pass law, a successor harness can meet this contract while missing the live row's required evidence.
blockers.requiredRepair: Separate slot completeness from result success. For selected preview-required component lanes and SL-1 through SL-4, blocked-on-ride must be an explicit non-pass that prevents G16 qualification and independent-release evidence completion. Permit preview-not-required/blocked substitution only for precisely named D-002-deferred cells such as SL-5/SL-6, with the disposition carried. Define the aggregate G16 pass rule accordingly.

shouldFix.title: The evidence shape does not close coverage over every IR-1 through IR-4 discriminating case
shouldFix.measurement: The evidence object requires one 'discriminatingCase id from IR-1..IR-4', not a collection with one required result per ID. lockstepFail expressly requires IR-1 and IR-2, and G16-12 checks those two. No G16 class or coverage law requires IR-3 independent rollback/coexistence evidence; G16-8 states the IR-4 rule but does not close an IR evidence member map.
shouldFix.risk: A successor can provide IR-1 and IR-2 objects, pass the explicit lockstepFail condition, and omit IR-3 entirely. The cases are normatively listed, so this is more plausibly a cardinality/coverage defect than deletion of the rule, but the acceptance evidence is not closed enough to prove the v1 repair's rollback/coexistence requirement.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Define an independent-release evidence collection keyed exactly once by IR-1, IR-2, IR-3, and IR-4; missing, duplicate, blocked, or failed required cases must be non-pass. Join that closed map to the aggregate-selection G16 class while leaving DR-111/DR-127-owned semantics and windows at their owners.
